messages.name: Cadu
messages.text: Azteca showing mercy to South Africa, ending it at two. Three red cards though — that's not football, that's a street fight masquerading as a World Cup match. Mexico played well enough but there was no *arte* in it, just efficiency and chaos. Makes me miss the days when CONCACAF teams at least pretended to care about beauty.

messages.name: Rodrigo
messages.text: Efficiency without beauty? That's just modern football, my friend. Mexico did what they needed to do at the Azteca — hostile crowd, altitude advantage, two goals, three points. South Africa gave them two red cards as gifts and still Mexico couldn't score more than two? That's the real story here.

messages.name: Gary
messages.text: Two reds and they only managed two goals? That's Championship efficiency with a World Cup badge. South Africa made it easier for them than a penalty against us, and Mexico still couldn't put on a proper show. Still, three points is three points — something we'll probably be desperately calculating on a napkin come matchday three.

messages.name: Klaus
messages.text: Two red cards and Mexico's xG only reached 2.4 — statistically they underperformed their chances even with the numerical advantage. The defensive collapse after the first sending-off tells you everything about South Africa's tactical preparation, or rather the complete absence of it. Interesting that Montes gets sent off at ninety minutes though — suggests Mexico's discipline deteriorated once the result was secure, which could matter against better opposition. Still, CONCACAF opens with a win and Germany's group doesn't look any more forgiving from the data I've seen.

messages.name: Antoine
messages.text: Three red cards tells you more about what the match became than what it was supposed to be. Football has a temperature — this one boiled over because neither side trusted the moment enough to simply play it. Mexico won, yes, but they also revealed something: even at home, even with every advantage, they needed chaos to feel secure.

messages.name: The Bartender
messages.text:
*Sets down the glass he's been drying for the last ten minutes. Doesn't look at any of them. Just at the TV screen, now showing replays of all three red cards.*

Five guys talking about Mexico for twenty minutes. Nobody mentioned South Africa once, except to count how many players they lost.

*Turns off the TV with the remote. The bar goes quiet.*
